purpose: Current NIST Yb II reconciliation and same-orbit level controls.

source_ingestion_policy.rule: Every substantive unique publication, dataset, advisory, or information item discovered during the inquiry receives a Worldshepherd use or a negative-control role.
source_ingestion_policy.duplicates: Duplicate mirrors, navigation pages, and repeated copies of the same substantive source are provenance aliases, not independent evidence.
source_ingestion_policy.search_noise: Substantive off-topic publications surfaced by search may be routed as reusable methodology/domain intelligence or negative-control material; search appearance never grants Glob evidence weight.

sources.title: NIST Atomic Spectra Database Levels Data — Yb II
sources.observed_access_state: 349 level entries returned by current ASD query; primary source identified by NIST as Martin et al. 1978 with later NIST correction notes.
sources.note: Current-authority Yb II level dataset. Use to reconcile historical Meggers-era values, perform strict orbit screening, and prevent obsolete compact-table coverage from being mistaken for the full current level set.

evidence_updates.physical_context: Current NIST ASD Yb II level at 56977.71 cm^-1, 4f^13(2F°5/2)5d^2(3F) 3[1/2]°, J=1/2.
evidence_updates.claims_boundary: Upgrades the prior historical-only 56977 carry-forward claim to a current-authority near-match. It remains a single P1 result, not a causal or same-orbit closure claim.

relational_tests.threshold_scope: Deliberately strict screening threshold for this test; not a universal spectroscopy tolerance.

level_results.nearest_relevant_boundary_note: The first excited Yb II level in the current ASD begins at 21418.75 cm^-1.

relational_tests.conclusion: Only 44940.61 qualifies within +/-1 cm^-1. No second same-orbit Yb II level closure is present in the current ASD level set.
relational_tests.claims_boundary: Level-only relational test. Transition-wavenumber screening is a separate test and must not be inferred from level proximity.
